chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Asim ibn Humayd from Abi Basir said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The people ate the meat of their beasts on the day of Khaybar, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) ordered that their pots be covered and forbade them from that, and he did not prohibit it before.
ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad permanently prohibit eating the meat of camels and other beasts during the Battle of Khaybar?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar clarifies the ruling on eating the meat of domestic donkeys (himir al-ahlia) by referencing the Battle of Khaybar, where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) permitted their consumption temporarily due to necessity but later prohibited it. The narration highlights the distinction between temporary permissibility (ja'iz) during times of need and permanent prohibition (haram), a key topic in Shia fiqh regarding the four-legged beasts other than cattle and camels.
